title: Effects of web-based concordancing instruction on EFL students’ learning of verb–noun collocations
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether web-based concordancing instruction can improve learners’ knowledge of English verb–noun collocations. The authors investigate five web-based practice units built around a Chinese–English bilingual concordancer (a keyword retrieval program) and ask whether repeated online exposure and practice help students learn collocations more effectively.

The participants were 32 college EFL students in Taiwan. They completed a pre-test, two post-tests, a background questionnaire, and an evaluation questionnaire. The study is an instructional intervention delivered in a web-based language-learning context, with performance tracked over time to see whether learning gains persisted after practice.

Results showed that students improved significantly immediately after the online practice, but some regression occurred later, although final performance remained above the entry level. The effectiveness of the instruction varied by collocation type and by learners’ prior collocation knowledge. Most participants found both the online instructional units and the concordancer acceptable. The study suggests that web-based concordancing can support collocation learning, but that gains may not fully endure without continued reinforcement.

identified_tools.name: CAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Computer-assisted language learning or instruction systems that provide digital practice, interaction, and/or automated feedback in language learning contexts.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a conference/program index entry and does not report an empirical study of a specific AI tool; it mentions web-based concordancing, virtual platforms, peer review, corpora, email, chat rooms, and related CALL practices in passing.

quality_tier_rationale: This is not a single empirical study of an AI tool; it is an index/listing of multiple language teaching and learning articles with brief summaries. No rigorous tool-specific methodology or outcome evidence is reported for a discrete system.
impact_tier_rationale: The excerpt contains no directly reported effect sizes or measured impact for a specific AI tool. At most, it suggests broad relevance of CALL/corpus-based practices, but the evidence is indirect and not attributable to one intervention.
